sections.title: Emergency treatment of high-risk pulmonary embolism
key_points: Primary reperfusion treatment (in most cases systemic thrombolysis) is the treatment of choice for patients with high-risk PE.

Surgical pulmonary embolectomy or percutaneous catheter-directed treatment are alternative reperfusion options for patients with contraindications to thrombolysis if appropriate expertise/resources are available.

After reperfusion and haemodynamic stabilization, patients can be switched from parenteral to oral anticoagulation; timing should be based on clinical judgement (patients in this risk category were excluded from phase III NOAC trials).

Follow specified higher initial dosing regimens for apixaban or rivaroxaban (apixaban for 1 week, rivaroxaban for 3 weeks after PE diagnosis specified here), or ensure a minimum overall period (5 days) of heparin anticoagulation before switching to dabigatran or edoxaban.
See supplementary data (Figure 1, Table 8) for management algorithms and tested/approved regimens.

sections.title: Treatment of intermediate-risk pulmonary embolism
key_points: For most acute PE without haemodynamic compromise, parenteral or oral anticoagulation (without reperfusion techniques) is adequate.
Normotensive patients with at least one indicator of elevated PE-related risk, or with aggravating conditions/comorbidity, should be hospitalized.
Patients with signs of RV dysfunction on imaging (echocardiography or CTPA) accompanied by positive troponin should be closely monitored for early haemodynamic decompensation/circulatory collapse.
Routine primary reperfusion (notably full-dose systemic thrombolysis) is not recommended because bleeding risk outweighs expected benefits.
Rescue thrombolytic therapy, or surgical embolectomy/percutaneous catheter-directed treatment, should be reserved for patients who develop haemodynamic instability.

PEITHO trial data cited for timing between randomization and death/haemodynamic decompensation; recommends reasonable practice to keep intermediate–high-risk PE patients on LMWH for first 2–3 days and ensure stability before switching to oral anticoagulation.
Same specifications as in high-risk section regarding increased initial dose of apixaban or rivaroxaban, or minimum overall heparin period before switching to dabigatran or edoxaban.

trials_and_references: phase III NOAC trials (patients in high-risk category were excluded)
PEITHO trial (time between randomization and death/haemodynamic decompensation cited)

monitoring_and_transition_advice.monitoring: Patients with RV dysfunction and positive troponin should be monitored over initial hours/days for haemodynamic decompensation.
monitoring_and_transition_advice.transition_from_parenteral_to_oral: Base timing on clinical judgement; follow drug-specific initial dosing regimens or minimum heparin duration (5 days) before switching to certain oral agents.
